page.description: Universal Blue editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A family of atomic Fedora desktop images built with bootc: Bluefin (GNOME), Aurora (KDE) and the gaming variant Bazzite. The system image is updated as a whole, with rollback to the previous deployment.
pros: Atomic image updates: a failed update can be rolled back at boot.
Fedora base with codecs, drivers and Flatpak set up from the first boot.
Several images (Bluefin GNOME, Aurora KDE) from the same build system.
Rebuilt on a frequent schedule, with signed images.
cons: Not a traditional package-by-package install: changes belong in containers or layers.
The Bazzite image has its own catalog entry; this page covers Bluefin.
The project publishes no SHA-256 list, so the digest here was computed by ROMinit.
No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed, so this page is logo-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for Universal Blue; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Write the ISO to a USB stick with dd or any image writer; writing erases the stick, and the installer then erases the target disk and deploys the image.
